source_read: https://www.wenzels.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Wenzels_Allergen_Sheet_June_2026.pdf (Allergen Sheet version 07, 19/06/2026, Last-Modified 22 Jun 2026; allergen matrix on pages 5-7, page 4 is photos). robots.txt only disallows /wp-json/ and /?rest_route=, Crawl-delay 10 honoured. Downloaded again once on 2026-10-09: sha256 99cdafd5985aa2ee4260afcb0a61e5d609f2238731058e09960c549fe5ba511f, identical to the file the data was built from, so checked_on stays 2026-10-08.
method: The matrix pages are three images (no text layer). tools/uk_extract/wenzels_matrix.py classifies every cell (Y / May / N) from pixels of the pdfimages extraction. Independent checks, none sharing that classifier: (1) the pages rendered with pdftoppm at 150 dpi, and 46 randomly chosen published rows (seed 20261009, about 36% of the 124 matrix rows tied to items; pages 5, 6 and 7, food and drinks) cropped with their name and the header band and compared by eye with allergens.csv, every non-N cell, 1,196 cells; (2) tesseract OCR of ALL 3,302 cells (6x upscale, single-character mode) and of all 127 row names, compared with the parser's words and with MATRIX_NAMES. Negative control: not run (the OCR result is an agreement count, see below).
ocr_non_N_cells_confirmed: 517 of 629 (226 Y, 291 May); the other 112 Y cells were not read by OCR (never contradicted)
names_ocr: 122 of 127 row names match MATRIX_NAMES at 0.8 similarity or better; 3 more match with the section bar text OCR picked up (Chicken Goujons, 4 Crusty Rolls, Mocha Frappe); 2 read as empty (Piri Piri Chicken Panini, Peri-Peri Chicken Pizza) and were confirmed by eye in the rendered page 5 (same rows, same positions)
held_back_detail: Policy 3 (2): White Tuna Salad Bloomer (its row marks no fish, while the Multiseed Tuna Salad Bloomer with the same filling is marked fish: the sheet contradicts itself) and Cherry Bakewell Tart (a Bakewell tart is made with almond, yet none of the eight tree-nut columns is marked; the Almond Madeira and Almond Muffin rows do mark almonds). The Cherry Bakewell holdback is a judgement call beyond the audit's name rules (its keyword list has no 'bakewell'): delete its entry in ALLERGEN_HOLDBACK in tools/uk_extract/wenzels.py to publish it. These two dishes get no allergens.csv row, so deleting the holdback line stops the build instead of publishing the row. The 16 dishes held back for their numbers keep their allergen rows (ignored while held).
audit: check_chain.py wenzels --fail-on-high: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 high, 0 medium audit flags. The published rows were also read by name for contradictions (cheese, mayo/aioli, tuna, egg, batter/crumb/bread/cake/pastry gluten, vegan, nut names): none besides the two held back. Roasted Chicken & Nduja Mayo Focaccia marks egg only as 'May' although its name says mayo; it is kept as printed because a warning is still shown (the audit counts may-contain as marked) and the row is a precautionary catch-all (may crustaceans, egg, fish, nuts...).
not_verifiable: The matrix prints no weights or serving sizes and one row (Belgian Bun) has no nutrition figures, so it is the only matrix row tied to no item. Rows for whole loaves and bloomers are as printed.
notes: may_contain_published = yes ('May' cells). Policy 2: a dish marked Y for wheat and May for rye/barley/oats publishes generic gluten (no named cereal); named cereals (wheat) appear only where no other cereal column is 'May'. Tree nuts named only where the sheet marks them (almond, pecan). The sheet's page 3 says everything is made where gluten, egg, milk, nuts, fish, mustard, celery, sesame, soya and sulphites are handled: a chain-wide statement, so it is in note.txt, not in the rows. The matrix spells two dishes differently from the nutrition page (Jam Donut / Iced England Donut vs Doughnut): the same recipe in the same position in both tables, handled by ALLERGEN_NAME_ALIAS.
